title: Weekly arXiv AI papers — 24–30 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. The ordering is inferred from current Hugging Face Papers upvotes in a limited sampled set; citation evidence for these recent papers is limited and was not used.

sections.title: ChronoReplay: One Answer Interface Is Not Enough for Streaming Spatial Intelligence
sections.abstract: ChronoReplay trains a spatial vision-language model on chronologically replayed, family-balanced supervision in native answer formats, and the authors report gains across three streaming-spatial benchmarks with additional inference-time gains from adaptive frame selection.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce interface lock-in for uneven transfer among categorical, metric, and temporal spatial answers, then report a single checkpoint improving OVO-S-Bench, OST-Bench, and UCS-Bench under matched observation access.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that their evaluation covers indoor scenes, leaving other environments untested.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 414 current Hugging Face Papers upvotes, highest among 73 eligible papers in sampled daily-paper lists; also ranked first with 131 community votes in the October 28 trendingai.today snapshot.

sections.title: The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
sections.abstract: The Trinity couples simulated-world generation with iterative agent-harness evolution around shared capabilities, reporting aggregate gains on training and unseen benchmarks, including two embodied tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors organize tasks into a capability tree and use Creator, Explorer, and Evolver roles to iteratively develop reusable harness modules; their paper reports mean gains of 34 points on 28 training benchmarks and 26 points on 18 unseen benchmarks.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say benchmark discovery relies on web search, whose coverage and result quality vary, and that this study focuses mainly on harness-level rather than model-parameter self-improvement.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 386 current Hugging Face Papers upvotes, second-highest among the eligible papers observed in the sampled lists.

sections.title: Multiscale Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
sections.abstract: MPO combines turn-level credit propagation and importance weighting with finer token-level credit assignment, reporting gains over reinforcement-learning baselines on search, tool-use, and automation tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose Multiscale Advantage Estimation and turn-level importance sampling, motivated by their observation that critic values vary mainly between assistant turns; reported experiments use 4B and 30B-A3B models.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evidence is limited to the paper’s search, tool-use, and automation tasks and those two model sizes; broader agent settings are not established by these experiments.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 380 current Hugging Face Papers upvotes, third-highest among the eligible papers in the sampled lists.

sections.title: Trajectory2Gym: Decision-Grounded Compositional Interaction Synthesis for Tool-Use Agents
sections.abstract: Trajectory2Gym synthesizes executable tool-use interactions with multi-step dependency coverage and trains only on actions supported by the information visible to the agent, reporting improvements across five Qwen3 scales.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors construct training interactions around under-supported compositional structures, certify actions against learner-visible history, and report a 16.9–29.8 percentage-point improvement in the equal-weight mean across Tau1, Tau2, and BFCL.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors describe matched 8B controls as directional evidence for design choices, with the clearest isolated gain attributed to parent normalization; this is not a full isolation of every component.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 367 current Hugging Face Papers upvotes, fourth-highest among the eligible papers in the sampled lists; a technical submission is also listed on OpenReview.

sections.title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
sections.abstract: StreamVibe introduces a benchmark, streaming vision-language model, and memory harness for proactive assistance from implicit and changing video-stream intent, reporting improvements in response quality, timing, and sustained interaction.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report StreamVibe-Bench with 4.1K evaluation samples and 85K training samples, plus a streaming model and persistent-intent harness; they report a 10.7% improvement over baselines in response timing/answer quality and a further 12.3% gain in sustained proactive interaction.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported improvements are benchmark results; the abstract does not establish reliability in deployed, real-world video-assistance settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 172 current Hugging Face Papers upvotes, fifth-highest among eligible papers in the sampled lists; version 2 was updated within the reporting window.

sections.title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
sections.abstract: Across evaluated conversational-memory settings, the authors find that many dedicated memory systems underperform naïve retrieval-augmented generation and define the competing gains and losses as memory benefit and memory tax.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors analyze memory’s net value relative to naïve RAG and trace losses to information faithfulness, accessibility, and robustness across backbones.
sections.unique_caveat: The negative-net-value finding is conditional on the evaluated tasks and the chosen naïve-RAG reference; it does not establish that all memory designs are inferior on all tasks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 151 current Hugging Face Papers upvotes, sixth-highest among the eligible papers in the sampled lists; the authors provide a public project page with experiment details.

sections.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
sections.abstract: PDRVLA adds a lightweight physical-dynamics module to condition robot actions without online video generation, reporting results on four simulation benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors predict future RGB, depth, and optical-flow features to derive physical tokens for action generation; reported success rates cover LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin 2.0, and SimplerEnv.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation is simulation-only in the four named benchmarks; the abstract does not report physical-robot validation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 145 current Hugging Face Papers upvotes, seventh-highest among the eligible papers in the sampled lists; its robotics, vision, and learning cross-listing broadens the application mix.

sections.title: DynaFlow: Learning Free-Form Multi-Agent Orchestration
sections.abstract: DynaFlow trains a main agent to decide when collaboration is needed and synthesize executable workflows that coordinate fixed sub-agents, reporting gains across six reasoning and retrieval benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors let the main model compose and execute task-specific sub-agent workflows, reporting 88.08% overall accuracy in forced-collaboration mode and a 10.90-point advantage over the strongest evaluated baseline with the same backbone.
sections.unique_caveat: Results cover six benchmarks and a forced-collaboration setting; the abstract does not establish that the learned policy is best when collaboration is optional in deployment.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 142 current Hugging Face Papers upvotes, eighth-highest among the eligible papers in the sampled lists.

sections.title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
sections.abstract: Hy-Nomas is an 8B diffusion video world model for multi-turn free-form text instructions and camera control, using causal attention and interaction-history conditioning to generate variable-length video segments.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine structured video captions, action-aware causal attention, a prompt enhancer, and a staged training curriculum; the abstract reports superior human-evaluation performance over existing world models and says code, weights, and benchmarks are released.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports a human-evaluation comparison without giving its sample size or quantitative effect, so the magnitude of the claimed advantage is not clear from the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 126 current Hugging Face Papers upvotes, tied with InteractiveWorld; its later first-submission timestamp (27 Oct versus 25 Oct) breaks the tie.

sections.title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
sections.abstract: InteractiveWorld provides a verifiable closed-loop environment and 120-task benchmark for egocentric assistants that guide a human actor, with the authors reporting low long-horizon guidance and planning scores among 12 tested MLLMs.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a state-scored, multi-turn benchmark in which the assistant instructs a human actor and the environment updates from the actor’s actions; even their strongest tested model reaches at most 20% on long-horizon guidance and 25% on planning.
sections.unique_caveat: The environment is a verifiable simulation of human assistance, so the reported scores do not by themselves establish behavior with real users.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 126 current Hugging Face Papers upvotes, tied with Hy-Nomas; the older first-submission date puts it after Hy-Nomas in the tie-break.
